classification.difficultyReason: Identify a strong negative linear association from four supplied scatterplots.

content.prompt: In which graph would the data have a correlation coefficient closest to $-0.9$?

spec.description: Four labelled scatterplots in source order A–D, each with six black points and plain axes without arrows, ticks, numbers or variable labels. Relative point positions are reconstructed from the printed image; coordinates are drawing coordinates, not numerical data.
spec.mathematics: A has no clear linear trend; B rises then falls; C has a strong positive linear trend; D has a strong negative linear trend.
spec.answerVisibility: All four option plots are permanent student-visible givens; the correct option appears only in the answer.

answer.worked: A correlation coefficient close to $-0.9$ indicates a strong negative linear association. Graph D has points lying close to a downward-sloping straight line. Correct answer: D.
